verdict.rationale: Railway's own docs promise a repo-connected, no-new-tools workflow: you connect a Git repo, it auto-detects settings from your code, YAML is optional, and every pull request gets its own preview. That covers the Git and framework parts of the story, but nothing in the pack shows integration with an existing CI pipeline, and editor support appears only through AI-agent/MCP connections. All evidence is vendor marketing with no hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: documented compatibility with existing CI systems, non-AI editor workflow support, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Connect your repo, Railway handles the rest. Auto-config, instant previews, no new tools to learn.
Every pull request gets its own preview. No surprises after merge.
Railway reads your code and sets the right settings, automatically.
Modify settings directly from the canvas. YAML optional.
Works with Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Copilot, Droid, OpenCode, Windsurf, and more.
